description: For each rating, count the distinct film titles that have at least one copy in inventory; keep the ratings above the average count, then return the sum of their counts and their average amount above the average.

d.request: For each film rating, count the distinct films having at least one copy in inventory, then among ratings where this count exceeds the overall average, return the sum of their counts and the mean distance each exceeds the overall average.
d.sql:
WITH rating_film_counts AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) as film_count
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(film_count) as avg_count
  FROM rating_film_counts
)
SELECT 
  SUM(rfc.film_count) as sum_of_counts,
  AVG(rfc.film_count - s.avg_count) as mean_distance_above_avg
FROM rating_film_counts rfc
CROSS JOIN stats s
WHERE rfc.film_count > s.avg_count

b.request: Count distinct films by rating that have at least one inventory copy; identify ratings above the average distinct film count; return the sum of distinct films across above-average ratings and the mean surplus by which above-average ratings exceed the overall mean count.
b.sql: WITH film_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) as distinct_films FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), avg_count AS (SELECT AVG(distinct_films) as avg_distinct FROM film_counts) SELECT SUM(fc.distinct_films) as sum_distinct_films, AVG(fc.distinct_films - ac.avg_distinct) as mean_surplus FROM film_counts fc CROSS JOIN avg_count ac WHERE fc.distinct_films > ac.avg_distinct
b.raw: Count distinct films by rating that have at least one inventory copy; identify ratings above the average distinct film count; return the sum of distinct films across above-average ratings and the mean surplus by which above-average ratings exceed the overall mean count.

a.request: For each film `rating`, count the distinct films that have at least one copy in inventory (each title once, however many copies). Which ratings have more such films than the average of these counts across all ratings? Give one row with the total number of those films across those above-average ratings and the average amount by which their counts exceed the across-rating average, unrounded.
a.sql:
WITH rating_counts AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS distinct_films
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
average_all AS (
  SELECT AVG(distinct_films) AS avg_count
  FROM rating_counts
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT rc.distinct_films, (rc.distinct_films - aa.avg_count) AS excess
  FROM rating_counts rc
  CROSS JOIN average_all aa
  WHERE rc.distinct_films > aa.avg_count
)
SELECT 
  SUM(distinct_films) AS total_films,
  AVG(excess) AS avg_excess
FROM above_average

c.request: Looking at the films we have in stock by `rating`, which ratings have more films in inventory than the average rating does? Give me a single row with the total films in stock across those above-average ratings and, on average, how far above the across-rating average they are (no rounding). For each rating, count the distinct film titles that have at least one copy in inventory; keep the ratings above the average count, then return the sum of their counts and their average amount above the average.
c.sql:
WITH rating_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    f.rating,
    COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS film_count
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
average_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(film_count) AS avg_count
  FROM rating_counts
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    rc.film_count,
    (rc.film_count - ac.avg_count) AS above_average_amount
  FROM rating_counts rc
  CROSS JOIN average_count ac
  WHERE rc.film_count > ac.avg_count
)
SELECT 
  SUM(film_count) AS total_films_in_stock,
  AVG(above_average_amount) AS avg_above_average
FROM above_average
